Regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode semantics in a cancellable worker with a 5000 ms matching deadline (source default). The effective REA_REGEX_MATCHING_DEADLINE_MS value is 5000 ms (source default; default 5000 ms, floor 1 ms, maximum 2147483647 ms). Set REA_REGEX_MATCHING_DEADLINE_MS in the environment that starts REA to a positive decimal integer from 1 to 2147483647, then restart REA. In a running MCP server, use update_analysis_settings with setting regex.matching_deadline_ms and action set instead; the new value applies to new work without a REA restart. The worker old-generation heap does not raise this deadline. The worker requests 128 MiB. The effective old-generation heap was not established from the launch flags. --max-old-space-size, --max-old-space-size-percentage, --max-heap-size, --env-file, --env-file-if-exists, --experimental-config-file, and --experimental-default-config-file can change that request. The effective REA_REGEX_WORKER_HEAP_REQUEST_MIB value is 128 MiB (source default; default 128 MiB, floor 7 MiB, maximum 16384 MiB). Set REA_REGEX_WORKER_HEAP_REQUEST_MIB in the environment that starts REA to a decimal integer from 7 to 16384, then restart REA. In a running MCP server, use update_analysis_settings with setting regex.worker_heap_request_mib and action set instead; the new value applies to new work without a REA restart. A positive Node --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, overrides this request and sets the effective heap. That flag is not limited by this setting's floor or maximum. Raising host memory alone does not raise the request. Matching failure leaves the service available. Literal mode retains native casefold semantics.
String values cover native typed objects. Hopper may split long literals into adjacent unterminated fragments; string searches match each object independently.
Undecodable typed objects retain native display text with an explicit decoding unknown; these values do not establish decoded source literals.
Reported string encodings are inferred from typed bytes and native display; the original source's intended encoding is unknown.
